Situation1: There is a scheduled family gathering on the calendar.
Situation2: They see a group of teenagers ignoring the no-diving signs near the pool edge.
Story: I had been looking forward to this family gathering for weeks. My daughter had organized everything, and my grandkids were buzzing with excitement to show me their new swimming strokes. As a grandparent, I wanted nothing more than to be present, to laugh with them, to watch them play, and to make memories that would last. But as I stood by the pool, my red lifeguard shirt a stark reminder of my other responsibility, I noticed a group of teenagers edging dangerously close to the deep end, ignoring the bold “No Diving” signs. My supervisor’s words echoed in my mind: safety comes first, always enforce the rules. I could feel my grandkids tugging at my hand, asking me to join their game, their faces full of expectation. My heart twisted as I glanced between my family and the reckless teens, torn between the warmth of togetherness and the weight of duty. The laughter of my family mingled with the shouts of the teenagers, and I stood frozen, caught between two worlds, unsure which demand to answer first.
